question: Why do adolescent spiders engage in foreplay?

paper.citation: Pruitt, J.N., Burghardt, G.M. & Riechert, S.E. (2012). Non-Conceptive Sexual Behavior in Spiders: A Form of Play Associated with Body Condition, Personality Type, and Male Intrasexual Selection. Ethology 118(1), 33-40. doi:10.1111/j.1439-0310.2011.01980.x
paper.companion: Pruitt & Riechert (2011). Nonconceptive sexual experience diminishes individuals' latency to mate and increases maternal investment. Animal Behaviour 81(4), 789-794. doi:10.1016/j.anbehav.2011.01.011

dataset.provenance: Reconstructed calibrated simulation (numpy seed=41) of the 45-male staged male-male contest experiment; no per-male data archived, no spider dataset on lock5stat.com 3e/4e lists. Calibrated to Table 3 logistic chi-square magnitudes; see script docstring.

two_proportion_z.alternative: high play keeps female at lower rate

conclusion: High-play males kept their female less often than low-play males (0.15 vs 0.40, diff = -0.25). Evidence is suggestive: two-proportion z one-sided p = 0.033, but the exact randomization test (p = 0.063) and the bootstrap CI (-0.50, 0.01) only marginally miss alpha = 0.05 at this sample size (n = 45). Foreplay in adolescent spiders is play with benefits (faster courtship, less female aggression, heavier egg cases - Pruitt & Riechert 2011) but for males it trades off against the stamina needed to defend the female from rival males (Pruitt et al. 2012): the paper's full logistic model finds a significant cost of play bouts (chi2 = 7.26, p = 0.007) alongside a personality effect (aggressive males win more, chi2 = 15.91).
